name: Supermicro GPU and HGX systems (8-GPU and 4-GPU nodes)
region: Worldwide; sold direct and through distributors (IT Creations, CDW and others carry Supermicro lines)
notes:
QUOTE-ONLY - Supermicro's accelerator pages carry a 'Request Pricing' contact form and no price. The value of this record is the node-level BASELINE, verified from the air-cooled GPU portfolio page, which groups its systems by accelerator rather than by SKU: 'NVIDIA HGX Blackwell and Blackwell Ultra' supporting HGX B200 and B300 (up to 8TB DDR5, 10x PCIe 5.0); 'AMD Instinct MI350X' (up to 6TB DDR5); an '8-10 PCIe GPU' class explicitly for 'AI Factories and Large-scale AI Inference' listing RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition / Max-Q, RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell Server Edition, AMD Instinct MI350P and NVIDIA H200 NVL; and a '2-6 PCIe GPU' class for enterprise and edge. Concrete example model verified: SYS-521GE-TNRT, a 5U dual-root PCIe system with up to 10 GPUs on the X13DEG-OA board, NVIDIA-Certified. KEY BASIS POINT for anyone budgeting: this class of box is where the accelerator COMES WITH THE SYSTEM. There is no Supermicro SKU 'one H200 SXM'. A published base-system price from a Supermicro channel would exclude GPUs entirely, so a 'Supermicro 5U server' price and a 'Supermicro 8xH200 node' price are not comparable and the former is a trap. Supermicro also builds AMD Helios rackscale.

 LEAD TIME: null and it is an EXPLICIT NEGATIVE, checked 2026-10-04. This is a quote-only channel - no price and no lead time is published on any page, and AGENTS.md forbids inventing an unsourced number, so the field stays null with the reason recorded. The negative is itself a procurement fact: a channel that will not state a lead time is a channel where the lead time is set by whatever allocation you happen to have, and it is exactly the kind of number to ask for in writing before signing. Probe log and per-vendor detail in source spl-negative-no-oem-publishes-lead-time; the one figure published anywhere in this chain is AWS's 8-week MAXIMUM Capacity Block booking horizon, which is a commitment ceiling rather than a delivery time.

 EXPORT CONTROL (2026-10-04, mechanism-level; sources spl-eccn-3a090-ccl, spl-bis-2026-01-advanced-computing-case-by-case, spl-bis-2026-05-d5-guidance). The ids on this record span both controlled and uncontrolled parts, which is exactly why this channel is recorded as controlled rather than left ambiguous. MI350X/MI350P/MI355X and HGX B200/B300 carry ECCN 3A090.a thresholds (TPP >= 4800, or TPP >= 1600 with performance density >= 5.92) and the January 2026 rule (91 FR 1684) names AMD MI325X as a worked example of the TPP < 21,000 / DRAM bandwidth < 6,500 GB/s band that moved from presumption of denial to case-by-case. RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition and H200 NVL sit on the professional/datacenter side of the consumer line and follow the die, not the brand. Three layers must be cleared: the US export licence; the 742.6(a)(6)(iii)(A) end-user and ultimate-parent test, which reaches entities HEADQUARTERED OR PARENTED in D:5 or Macau even when the entity itself is outside those groups; and the surviving presumption of denial on reexports, in-country transfers and to D:5/Macau buyers. THE BASIS POINT ALREADY IN THIS RECORD IS ALSO THE CONTROL POINT: because at this channel the accelerator comes WITH the system, there is no Supermicro SKU 'one H200 SXM', so the exportable item is a system containing controlled silicon - the licence analysis and the price basis are both determined by that same packaging.
